title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

title: Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Meanwhile King Oceiros, consumed by his search for a worthy heir and driven to madness, would abandon the government to try to transform himself into a dragon, condemning the kingdom to the consequences of the fading of the Flame, as well as the chaos of a war of faith among the ranks of the army.

When the First Flame began to fade and the time came for Prince Lothric to fulfill his destiny and become a Lord of Cinder, he refused the call. After reflecting on his mentor's teachings, the state of the kingdom and the world, his accursed life, and the atrocities committed for the Flame, the prince denounced the legacy of the Lords, and chose to await the Flame's death from the distance. Unable and unwilling to fulfill their destiny, the princes retreated to their chambers atop Lothric Castle to await the end of the world, protected by their royal guard and Lion Knight Albert, Black Hand Kamui and Daughter of Crystal Kriemhild.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, the First Flame is so weakened that Lords of Cinder past are resurrected so that the embers of the First Flame inside them serve as fuel for new Linkings. Prince Lothric, who was raised to become the next Lord of Cinder, refused to Link the First Flame, while three of the resurrected Lords of Cinder refused to be used as fuel, leading to resurrection of several Unkindled in the hopes that one of them might slay the fleeting Lords of Cinder and Lothric, and Link the First Flame.

These beings will possess fragments of the First Flame stored within their bodies in the form of cinders, giving them the powers of the Flame in a world that will be enveloped in Darkness.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : The Lords of Cinder are beings that have linked the First Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire through the centuries. Although many of these champions have followed the sacrifice of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, not everyone became a Lord of Cinder through heroic deeds or even of free will. One such case is Aldrich, who became a Lord only because he had the strength to become one, despite having obtained such power by devouring an untold number of humans for his own pleasure.

The continuous linking of the Flame eventually culminated in the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who linked the Flame throughout history. This being, although appearing as an empty husk, inherits the abilities of the Lords of Cinders who have come before. It has long existed as the Flame's last defense inside the Kiln, protecting it from Champions attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength.

title: Firelink Shrine (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The opening area is a large circular chamber where five great thrones face a central bonfire, the only bonfire guarded by a Firekeeper in the whole game. Each of the five thrones looks different and unique, fitting the Lord of Cinder it is made for: The first draped with a extravagant red cloth and covered in saintly candles; the next plain and lightly decorated; the center is heavily charred with molten streaks and half-melted features; the next is flanked with a number of swords besides it; and the final is much too large for any normal human to sit upon. All of these thrones (save the second) are missing their respective Lords, and thus the Unkindled must find them and force their cinders to be seated.

Below the main entrance is a tunnel that leads to a back chamber. The Shrine Handmaid sells goods here, and Blacksmith Andre smiths goods here. Throughout the journey, the Unkindled can recruit a number of vendors and tutors to get new gear and learn new spells.

title: Lothric
snippet: The new inhabitants of the region soon found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns and had to rise to the challenge, ascending common knighthood. The old knights of Lothric turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, and built an altar for him in their city, beginning to worship the ancient deity who in return gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: Lothric
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who would sacrifice himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he would fulfill his destiny. Oceiros created extensive propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance. However, the hopes of the royal family would soon fade, as Lothric remained a shriveled child from birth into adulthood, never even growing out of his baby clothes.

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

snippet: Due to the Convergence, a massive seismic upheaval raised the Lothric plateau high above the land, cutting it off from its neighbouring regions. This new feature was called the High Wall, and removed all means of transportation in or out of the city. Lothric messengers had no means of returning, and pilgrims of Londor were unable to seek refuge, leading to the total isolation of the kingdom during its final days. The Stray Demon that was once the gatekeeper of Lothric would remain trapped on the kingdom's broken bridge, without even a trace of its flame.

title: Lothric
snippet: The fading of the Flame and the erosion of their faith made the citizens of Lothric more and more desperate, some of whom were transformed into humanoid trees that were turned in prayer towards Lothric Castle. Furthermore, the undead of the city began to show signs of an epidemic, in which their Dark Soul would explode from their bodies and manifest as an amorphous black blob with bestial features which attacked anything with destructive ferocity. The infestation of these Pus of Man led to the permanent closure of the Grand Archives' doors, with the scholars isolating themselves from the desperate situation of the kingdom to continue their work.

title: Sister Friede

Among the resurrected Unkindled was Elfriede, who instead chose to renounce everything, leaving behind her role as leader of the Sable Church, Londor, and even her name, becoming known simply as "Friede". Left without a home, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, where the forlorn and the outcast were welcomed and found refuge. Friede became the first Ashen One to reside in it, coming to accept the cold of the Painted World and considering it her new home. She discovered that she wanted to "protect" the inhabitants of the Painted World, and thus assumed the precise form that they yearned for: that of their former mistress Priscilla. title: Lothric
snippet: As the kingdom of Lothric found itself managing the system of Firelinking,**** coupled with their subscription to the Way of Blue faith, it inevitably came into contact with Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Ruled by Gwyndolin, the king of the gods, Irithyll and Lothric recognized a common ground in their Firelinking legacy, as well as their faith which venerated the moon god. Soon after, the two kingdoms established diplomatic relations: the scholars and knights of Lothric would travel to Irithyll, and Lothric knights would adopt crossbows that used lightning bolts produced by the giant blacksmiths of Anor Londo. The Boreal Valley also became a place of pilgrimage for the knights of Lothric, who sought to reach the residence of their patron deity in Archdragon Peak through meditation.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Calling it "futile" is a euphemism: the unnatural prolonging of the First Flame's lifespan came with disastrous, if not, downright catastrophical proportions: when the Lords of Cinder started to resurrect, somehow, portions of their countries and homelands were, literally, "teleported" to Lothric, changing the landscape in unpredictable ways.

By the time *Dark Souls 3* takes place, the damage caused to the world by the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire seems to be irreversible.

As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet: Even after possibly hundreds of thousands years after the first linking of the Flame, Frampt (or other serpents affiliated with his ideology) continued to propagate the cult of the linking of the Flame; influencing kingdoms, rulers and simple Undead to continue the tradition started by Gwyn. When the First Flame drifted up to position itself on the nascent kingdom of Lothric, Frampt or other serpents affiliated with his ideology reached the city too. Over time the serpents passed on the culture of linking the Flame to the royal family of Lothric, pushing them to preserve the tradition and actively produce heirs capable of becoming Lords of Cinder. Frampt or his kin were represented in numerous statues, on par with the Three Pillars of Lothric, with elegant clothes and angel wings, showing their central role within the kingdom, considered "divine messengers". In this strange realm, the Firelink Shrine had no fire, and Gundyr ended up arriving "late" for the celebrations that awaited his fate. title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In *Dark Souls III*, countless beings have prolonged the Age of Fire, preventing its end and holding off the coming of the Age of Dark. By the time the game begins, there are countless Lords of Cinder - those who successfully linked the First Flame before - and even more Unkindled who were unsuccessful. Eventually the one anointed to next link the Flame (and indeed, who was born for that very purpose), Prince Lothric, rejected the idea that the Age of Fire should be prolonged any further and instead desired to end what he called the "fire-linking curse." A contingency plan was then activated, in which previous Lords of Cinder were resurrected in hopes that they, who had linked the First Flame before, might do so again. However, by this time, the world that had been created during the Age of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. title: Humans
snippet:
Humans -  Dark Souls III - character - last_days_of_fire 
 last_days_of_fire : Many millennia—or even more—have gone by, and the linking of the Fire has become a staple in the world. Finally, when the new "Lord of Cinder" Prince Lothric was destined to sacrifice himself to the Flame, he refused and opted to watch the Age of Dark settle. To save the Age of Gods, four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected as Undead, but three of them either sought the Age of Dark, or no longer cared either way. One last contingency plan existed, to awaken the Unkindled, those who had previously failed to prolong the Age of Fire with their sacrifices. Kaathe's will has been reinterpreted by the Sable Church of Londor, who aim for a different Age of Dark than what Kaathe sought; an age ruled by a Lord of Hollows.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who was tasked with sacrificing himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince to the Kiln of the First Flame, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he was ready to fulfill his destiny.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: When the royal family realized that Lothric would not improve from his condition, they resorted to repulsive acts in an attempt to obtain a worthy Champion for the linking, even if it meant to create something inhuman: the rulers bound the souls of the two princes together with a curse. Although the exact motive behind this act is unknown, it is likely that the rulers intended for Prince Lothric to draw out some of the strength of his elder brother's soul, potentially making them worthy Champions for the First Flame together. The resulting Soul of the Twin Princes was suitable kindling for the First Flame, even as the princes were physically incapable of overcoming the obstacles involved in linking the Flame. Unable and unwilling to fulfill their destiny, the princes retreated to their chamber to await the end of the world.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Among them was Aldrich who, like the other exhumed Lords, had no intention of sacrificing himself again, as his reflections on the state of the world had led him to understand that an Age of the Deep would soon arrive, motivating him to devour the gods themselves, in order to erode their hold on the Flame and accelerate the coming of his vision. Gathering an army of deacons from the Cathedral of the Deep led by Archdeacon McDonnell, Aldrich would march on Irithyll, intent on capturing Anor Londo to devour the king of the gods himself. However, he would find his way blocked by Sulyvahn and his knights, as the Pontiff had no intention of relinquishing the source of his control over the city and the Way of White so easily. From the ensuing battle Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and defeating

title: Angel
snippet: As the pilgrims of Londor were sent to Lothric with the objective to die some of them died and turned into "angels". One day one of them managed to visit Gertrude, the holy maiden of Gwynevere, Queen of Lothric and it revealed to her a truth capable of manifesting pillars of light together with a heretic tale. The holy maiden was convinced by this enlightenment and began to spread the worship of those she considered "divine messengers". However this faith was viewed as heresy in Lothric, as it opposed the worship of the ancient gods and the duty to continue linking the First Flame and was consequently unrecognized by any of the Three Pillars that govern the realm, leading to a civil war inside the walls of Lothric between the Winged Knights that followed Gertrude's faith and the Angels and those still loyal to the Pillars.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: Like humanity and the Gods of Anor Londo of old, the demons seek to rekindle the Flame of Chaos to preserve their race. A Demon Prince, a champion of their race, challenged Prince Lorian of Lothric, only to be defeated and retreat without his memory of the flames. No longer able to pursue the rekindling of the Chaos Flame, the demon race was condemned to extinction; as time went on, even the few remaining demons all but lacked any trace of the flame within; one such lost demon, reduced to little more than a wood and stone golem, served as a gatekeeper of Lothric.

title: Gertrude
snippet: Some of Gertrude's knights possibly attempted to reach the chambers of Prince Lothric to either kill him and prevent any Unkindled from recovering his Cinders, or convert him to have him help usher an Age of Dark; their attempts were unsuccessful as any intruders were killed by his brother Lorian. The room of the bossfight of Lothric and Lorian is covered by large, white feathers, the only creatures known to possess such wings and that could come so far into the prince's chambers being the Winged Knights and the Knights of Gertrude. The presence of a large number of Lothric knights and battle-scarred barricades before the prince's chamber, directly facing the structures presided over by the Winged Knights, also suggests a recent fight between the two groups.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: In the final days of Lothric, the citizens of the kingdom forgot even the miracles of the goddess of sunlight, and ended up recounting childish but earnest stories to try to recall her blessings and the back of her figure, as the last image of their queen before she left.

title: Lore
snippet:
Gwyn, in a final effort to save the Age of Fire, marches with a great deal of his army to the Kiln of the First Flame and sacrifices himself to link with the First Flame, turning the Kiln to ash and incinerating his entire army (making them the Black Knights, who later walk Lordran). The attempt is temporarily successful, however, as the Age of Fire was only extended for at least 1000 years. Gwyn became a Hollow and is from then on known as "Gwyn, Lord of Cinder".

The Four Kings became corrupted and were seduced by evil at some point by Kaathe after Gwyn's fall and their servants turned into Darkwraiths. In an effort to stop them New Londo was flooded with all of its population, trapping the Four Kings with their Darkwraiths in the Abyss.

Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet: When the First Flame once again began to fade and the previous Lords of Cinder refused to serve as kindling again, the Unkindled buried in the Cemetery of Ash were resurrected. The remains of Gundyr's golem became the judge of these potential champions trying to reach Firelink Shrine. However, after his lifetime of service, the fire that was burned into Gundyr by the Coiled Sword had died down, leaving him open to the pus of man overtaking his body. In his final battle, Iudex Gundyr's raging humanity would erupt in a violent outbreak of dark pus, driven by an untamable fury.

title: Courland
snippet: At a certain point the First Flame began to fade again and the first Fire Keeper of Lothric had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a "barren plane of endless darkness". For this reason, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition, was called to become a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Defying his frail appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Champion, something for which he himself expresses remorse and asks to be forgiven. Despite his role, Ludleth was then exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric, ensuring that the first Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes and that all future maidens like her were deprived of their sight, to prevent them from observing the future without the light of the First Flame. The original eyes were hidden in a version of the Firelink Shrine on the verge of sinking into darkness and where the First Flame was an

title: Deacons of the Deep
snippet: When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

title: Vordt of the Boreal Valley
snippet: After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Vordt was sent to Lothric with a division of Boreal Outrider Knights, with orders to keep a watchful eye over the Dancer of the Boreal Valley. Here he positioned himself to guard the main gate leading inside the city. Like other Outrider Knights, he would end up transformed by the rings of the Pontiff into a frenzied beast, causing his armor to be fused with his hide.

title: Dark Lord
snippet:
Dark Lord -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations**

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: She eventually became wife to King Oceiros, the last monarch of Lothric, and supported the kingdom's desire to produce an heir worthy of linking the First Flame, giving birth first to Elder Prince Lorian, raised to become a knight, and Younger Prince Lothric, expected to become a "champion" and sacrifice himself to the Flame. However, when Prince Lothric and his brother refused to link the fading Flame and they chose to wait out the end of the Age of Fire, King Oceiros went mad in his attempt to produce an heir worthy of their sacrificial destiny. The king discovered the heretical faith of the paledrake Seath among the scholars of the Grand Archives and became convinced that a crossbreed heir would have the strength to link the Flame. Oceiros eventually became a deformed humanoid dragon and with him the queen had her youngest child, Ocelotte. After producing the potential champion, Gwynevere quietly disappeared from the kingdom of Lothric. Realizing that the Flame would soon go out

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet: Eventually, the Watchers linked the Fire, although it is unknown if one or all had done so. With the Watchers becoming Lords of Cinder, the wolf blood dried up. The Followers, now having nothing to live for, went hollow, roaming the land and eventually disappearing into the Painted World of Ariandel. With no one remaining to execute the corrupted, the acolytes were slowly devolved by the Abyss, and Farron was consumed in a rotting bog. When the Abyss Watchers were awakened to kindle the Flame once again, they returned home to find it corrupted and their mission unsuccessful. The Watchers in the keep now fight against themselves, endlessly slaying their brethren corrupted by the Abyss.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: Archtree
snippet: At some point the creatures that found the Lord Souls near the First Flame underground and developed their powers emerged to the surface with the intention of exterminating the Dragons and conquer the world for themselves. During the war that followed, Izalith and her daughters used sorcery and their powers to manipulate flames and weaved great firestorms that scorched the very earth, destroying the archtrees and burning the dragons while Nito unleashed a miasma of death, rotting the archtrees and infecting the dragons and Gwyn and his knights battled the dragons with their their mighty lightning bolts. After the long struggle the Lords emerged victorious, exterminating most of the archdragons and archtrees, thus conquering the surface world for themselves.

title: Lindelt
snippet: Thanks to their well-honed miracles and unwavering faith in the face of death, the cleric knights of the Archdrake Church were a formidable force on the battlefield, even managing to stand up to the army of King Vendrick as worthy rivals. Miracles like Replenishment and Resplendent Life allowed the knights to endure and heal from arduous battles. Among the high-ranked clerics, Forsalle stood out thanks to his mastery of miracles, and led many battles across his country's borders. He earned the title of "holy knight" and was feared for his "demonic power" by his enemies. However, some cleric knights of Lindelt defected to escape their country's authoritarian rule. These clerics tried to start new lives in the destroyed kingdom of Drangleic and found their way inside the Shrine of Amana, where some of them went hollow.

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet: Considering that those who had deceived Gundyr had given him his halberd and charged him with linking the Flame, they must have had a position superior to the king of Lothric but still close to him. This could point to the involvement of Gwyndolin, king of the gods of Irithyll, who had strong ties to Lothric; or the Primordial Serpents, who were already advisors to the royal family. Using Gundyr as a golem to test the strength of future Champions would ensure that those overseeing the linking of the Flame would be guaranteed to find potential Lords with enough power to prolong the Age of Fire.

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: After their King was consumed by Chaos, many of Eleum Loyce's faithful knights decided to follow him and put him out of his misery, as his orders were to eliminate each malformed terror that arose from the flame, and they would thus not hesitate even it were their own leader. Sir Fabian led the loyal knights straight into the depths of the Old Chaos to exterminate its terrors one last time, however the mission proved to be a failure and not one of the selfless knights returned. The souls of the knights were taken by Chaos and corrupted, leading them to lose all sense of purpose and being, left in them driven only by the urge of expuning any who might disturb the flames, even if they were former compatriots. With their armor charred and burnt black by fire and still burning in agony they remained as empty shells controlled by the Chaos alongside their once-proud king. However a few woeful suls were able to sneak back home guided by the last faint vestige of self.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: of the resurrected Lords of Cinder, Aldrich had no intention of sacrificing himself anew, as he had come to believe that an "Age of the Deep" should come and replace the Age of Fire, motivating him to try to devour the gods themselves to erode their hold on the Flame and accelerate the coming of his vision. Gathering an army of deacons from the Cathedral of the Deep, Aldrich, still hungry for flesh and now eager to devour Gods, marched on Irithyll with his followers so that he could devour Gwyndolin, the king of the Gods. He found his way blocked by Sulyvahn and his knights, as the Pontiff had no intention of relinquishing the source of his control over the city and the Way of White without a fight. Aldrich emerged victorious from the ensuing battle, slaughtering Sulyvahn\'s troops and forcing the Pontiff to reluctantly clear the way for the ruined cathedral of Anor Londo. Having finally reached his prey, Aldrich began to slowly devour Gwyndolin, who was most likely powerless to fight

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet: However the flames of Chaos would not be sated, and over time the Ivory Knight was drained of his vigour and, sensing the degradation of his power he decided to plunge into Chaos' heart in an attempt to reduce its flames alone. However he was devoured by the chaos, becoming an empty husk controlled by it. After their King was consumed by Chaos, many of Eleum Loyce's faithful knights decided to follow him and put him out of his misery but their souls too were corrupted by the flames, leading them to lose all sense of purpose and being. They were then driven only by the urge of expunging any who might disturb the flames, even if they were former compatriots. With their armor charred and burnt black by fire and still burning in agony, they remained as empty shells controlled by the Chaos alongside their once-proud king.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

Once Aldrich defeated Sulyvahn and took control of the city, McDonnell remained to watch over the old Cathedral where the saint was busy digesting Gwyndolin, establishing the covenant of Aldrich Faithful, passing on his dark sorceries to followers who brought him evidence of success in their task.

title: Drangleic
snippet: fire of souls was not enough to harness the curse, and how the Flame would soon fade and the souls of ancient beings would reemerge, before Dark would descend as a curse on humans, making them take their true, immortal form. With the fire extinguished men would finally regain their true form and bury the shackles that the gods imposed on them. Yet he continued to look for an alternative, a way to maintain the world and life as it had always been, frightened by a future of Dark. As the kingdom was on the verge of being overwhelmed by the Giant Lord's offensive, King Vendrick disappeared. As every last attempt to purge the curse of Undeath had failed, he understood that the only solution available was to link the Fire himself, sacrificing his immense soul to temporarily eliminate the undead curse and give a glimmer of hope to his ruined kingdom.

title: Four Kings
snippet: Having failed to eliminate the dark threat, an agonizing and terrible decision was made: flooding the entire land of New Londo despite the realization that countless lives and the rich culture of the country would be lost. For this task, sorcerers were called, and the feat was accomplished without even evacuating the city's civilians, sealing away the Four Kings, their Darkwraiths and the entire population with them. The victims were thus cursed, and became Ghosts roaming the ruins of their country, seeking to make mincemeat of every living being.

title: Timeline
snippet:
These humanoid larvae are harmless on their own but are capable of manifesting and controlling bodies equipped with large shiny wings and capable of striking with overwhelming power
These "angels" reach Lothric and come into contact with Gertrude, the Queen's maid, and reveal a heretical doctrine to her, announcing the end of the Age of Fire
Dozens of these "angels" continue to try to reach Lothric's castle but all end up killed by his brother

title: Necromancer (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
At some point, these individuals would die, and therefore were affected by Undeath.

When some of the Iron King's soldiers tried to desert, perhaps when their situation started to become dire, the Necromancers put them down and revived them as skeletons, forcing them to serve anyway.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: the Four Kings and close the Abyss of New Londo. Following Artorias's failure, an agonizing and terrible decision was made in order to contain the Abyss: flooding the entirety of New Londo, despite the realization that countless lives would be lost along with its prosperous culture. For this task, sorcerers were called forth and the feat was accomplished without evacuating the city's civilians, sealing away the Four Kings, their Darkwraiths and the entire population with them. The victims were cursed and became Ghosts roaming the ruins of their country.

title: Timeline
snippet:
Yhorm, as one of the previous Lords of Cinder, is exhumed from his graves to use the embers of the Flame still within him as fuel for it
Yhorm refuses to contribute to the linking of the Flame once again and instead returns to the Profaned Capital
Yhorm remains on his throne inside the city's ruins to prevent further disastrous uses of the Profaned Flame

title: Sen's Fortress
snippet: Centuries after Lord Gwyn's sacrifice, as the First Flame began to fade and the curse of Undeath to regain strength heroes and warriors from all different lands tried to reach Lordran and ventured to Sen's Fortress to try and reach Anor Londo. Very few were successful, like the strongest Berenike Knight known as Black Iron Tarkus and a Warrior of Sunlight known as Solaire of Astora. However, most of them failed in their mission to conquer the fortress's challenges despite their multiple attempts over the decades, ending up trapped, hollow or only became additional roadblocks to further hinder future warriors.

title: Dark Soul
snippet:
Most Humans would come to serve the Gods in the years that followed, while their ancestors, the Pygmies and their royal family, were relocated to the Ringed City, “gifted” to them by the "generous" Lord Gwyn. He also gave to them his youngest daughter, Filianore, and as she was given away, her father promised the Princess that he would come back for her, one day.

Those royal pygmies that retreated to the Ringed City brought the Dark Soul with them, with the original soul eventually ending up split among multiple Pygmy Lords. The majority of the royals of the Pygmies continued to serve and revere the gods for millennia, but the Ringed Knights that took parts in the ancient war against the dragons subtly defied them in what ways they could.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: However, the rest of the firstborn's reign was marked by catastrophes. The Four Kings of New Londo were corrupted by the dark power of Darkstalker Kaathe, starting to sow devastation nearby the city of the gods. Following Knight Artorias's failure to defeat the Darkwraiths, the gods were forced to flood the city, sacrificing all the humans within, and seal it. A similar event happened in Oolacile when, again due to Kaathe, the awakening of the primordial human Manus and his fury led to the collapse of the country when Artorias was unable to defeat him. In addition to the grave situation on the borders of Anor Londo, the city of the gods itself became a dangerous place when a group of cultists began targeting the clan of Gwyn and their kind, and occult weapons capable of killing the gods reached inside the walls of Anor Londo. Furthermore, in the city of the gods Seath the Scaleless had now completely lost his mind, transforming his Archives into a prison and going so far as to kidnap

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: In the last days of Lothric, as the First Flame was almost faded, flocks of Pilgrim Butterflies would manifest in the Lothric skies. These gigantic humanoid insects with immense, branch-like wings would infest the skies of the dying kingdom, migrating towards the tip of Lothric Castle. Here they would take control of the statue of a Dragonslayer Armour through dark magic, using it as a puppet to eliminate anyone who attempted to proceed to the top of the castle.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: When Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Emma, the High Priestess of Lothric, would send out messengers bearing the banner of Lothric to ask allied countries for aid in resolving their internal situation. Sulyvahn would respond to his ally's call, ordering his Dancer to serve as a Boreal Outrider Knight in Lothric alongside a division of Boreal Outrider Knights, under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here she positioned herself to guard the Cathedral and High Priestess Emma while Vordt guarded the main gate of the city and the Outrider Knights infiltrated inside and around the city of Lothric.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - lothric_castle_and_the_consumed_king_s_garden 
 lothric_castle_and_the_consumed_king_s_garden : The Castle, home to various knights and soldiers of Lothric along with fire-breathing wyverns, holds the final Lord of Cinder. By now, the very sun itself resembles a Darksign, and Pilgrim Butterflies are seen flying towards the castle. Fighting their way through the castle, the Ashen One may choose to make a detour to the Consumed King's Garden, home to the king of Lothric, Oceiros. The king, having gone mad long ago and deformed himself into a dragon-like being, ferociously attacks the Ashen One.

title: Timeline
snippet:
An old armor of the ancient dragonslayers remains as a monument near the city barracks
The kingdom of Lothric builds an incredible army of skilled knights assisted by the wyverns they were able to tame
The kingdom of Lothric annihilates every other kingdom that drifts on its borders for centuries
---Lothric's knight become dragon worshipper---

title: Allfather Lloyd
snippet: Some of the dethroned god's followers, now cast out from the reformed faith, would find refuge in the Painted World of Ariandel, bringing with them the lost miracles of the old religion and fully believing that one day the aureoles of light associated with Lloyd would return with him. It's possible that Slave Knight Gael was once such a believer, due to his usage of that very miracle. That is in spite of his nature as a cursed Undead, which the old god seemingly despised.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: Oceiros created immense propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance. In a betrayal of the hopes placed in him, Lothric remained a sick and shriveled child from birth into adulthood, never even growing out of his baby clothes, which remained his only clothing throughout his life and were blessed to at least try to keep him healthy. In his youth, Aldia, the first of the Grand Archives scholars, became his mentor in secret, a likely influence on the young and impressionable prince, with whom he would have imparted his skepticism on the nature of the Age of Fire.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: The societal collapse of Izalith, left without their Lord and devoured by the out-of-control Flame of Chaos, pushed Gwyn to wage war against the chaos demons that were now free, developing weapons and fighting techniques strong enough to face the size of their new enemies and sending his Silver Knights to Izalith. During the war their armor and weapons were charred black but despite their strength Gwyn's knights failed to defeat the demons or destroy the Bed of Chaos; they eventually retreated, only managing to banish the demons underground although they enslaved some lesser demons who would become servants of the gods. At some point after Gwyn linked the First Flame and Gwyn's firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, nearly all of the other deities abandoned Anor Londo. Despite the conflict, many demons survived, and the Bed of Chaos meanwhile continued to generate new demons; with no leadership present in Anor Londo and the Silver Knights remaining relegated to protecting the city of

title: The Old Chaos
snippet: The king made some attempts to combat the Chaos, and his knights delved valiantly into the depths to exterminate the terrible things that dwelled there, but not one of them returned. Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce. He traveled deep into the Chaos with his knights until he was devoured by the flames.

title: Gertrude
snippet: Whatever the Angels communicated to Gertrude might have been the announcement of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of the Age of Dark, justifying the Kingdom's violent reaction. Given that Lothric culture essentially evolved around Firelinking, the Three Pillars had a stake in denouncing the revelations of the Angels who traced their roots to Londor, a realm devoted to bringing about an Age of Dark. Furthermore, the apparent ability of the Angel's miracle being able to manifest "light", counterintuitive to the Angels' somber origins, could have suggested that a world without flame would not be as "dark" as the Three Pillars would have Lothric believe.

title: Carthus of the Sands
snippet: At some point, the giant humanoid Wolnir rose to power in Carthus. The warriors of Carthus swore their lives to Wolnir, growing ever ruthless and bloody in his name. Under Wolnir's rule, the kingdom of Carthus grew aggressive and expansionist, to the point where it was likened to uncontrollable fire, its beacons being used as war signals. His conquests were spearheaded by his warriors with superior combat skills and combat pyromancies. Wolnir soon subjugated the kingdoms around Carthus, melding the various "crowns" that ruled different lands into a single one, thus ascending to "High Lord". Along the way, Wolnir stripped three armlets and a holy sword from the corpses of some clerics, demonstrating how religion and gods counted for nothing in his kingdom.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The **Ashen One,** also referred to as the **Champion of Ash** or **the Unkindled One,** is the playable character and the protagonist of *Dark Souls III*.

The title of Ashen One is given to the player by the Fire Keeper of Firelink Shrine. The Ashen One is an Unkindled, an Undead who failed to link the First Flame and became ash, who has been raised from their grave, and is tasked with a journey to defeat four Lords of Cinder and return them to their thrones, since the link of the Flame is threatened and the Lords refuse to serve as its fuel once again.

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - location 
 location : The Soul of Cinder can be reached after placing all Cinders of Lords upon their thrones and talking to the Fire Keeper, who will transport the Ashen One to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - soul_of_cinder 
 soul_of_cinder : After returning to the shrine, the Ashen One places the ashes of the Lords on their thrones, and the Firekeeper channels their strength to the Ashen One. The Firekeeper bids the Ashen One travel to the First Flame. Accepting the strength of the Lords, the Ashen One is transported to a copy of the Firelink shrine, standing amid the wreckage of kingdoms. From there, the Ashen One proceeds to the Kiln of the First Flame.

There they encounter the Soul of Cinder, a manifestation of the Lords that had previously linked the flame. The Soul of Cinder takes on many forms and fighting styles, mimicking those who had linked the flame. Once the Ashen One weakens it, the Soul of Cinder assumes the style of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, first one to link the flame. After defeating the Soul of Cinder, the Ashen One is presented with four options depending on the choices they made.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - hornet_ring 
 hornet_ring : Engraved with a hornet, the Hornet Ring belonged to Lord's Blade Ciaran. Increasing the power of critical attacks, it allows its wearer to lay waste to their foes much like how Ciaran did to Lord Gwyn's enemies.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - furtive_pygmy 
 furtive_pygmy : Unlike the other Lords, the Dark Soul did not have any instantly apparent effect on the Pygmy. They appear to have looked like a generic hollow before claiming their soul.

The Furtive Pygmy's ultimate role, actions, and fate are largely unknown. He is mostly forgotten, save for adherents of Kaathe and some inhabitants of the Ringed City.

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
During the second phase, he can roll and dodge ranged attacks.
The Soul of Cinder has a fifth weapon style that goes unused, involving a greatsword. It covers both the body of the Soul of Cinder and the weapon in flames much like his final phase (for a video see here: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ruKjgqhUr4A&t=14m50s). Whether it was part of its first phase, second phase, or something in-between is unknown.
Due to how the Soul of Cinder took on Gwyn's moveset and persona for his second phase, it could be inferred that one's prominence within the Soul of Cinder is related to the strength of their soul. This could also explain why the Soul of Cinder's armor strongly resembles the Elite Knight Set that the Chosen Undead was depicted as wearing in most *Dark Souls* art; as the Chosen Undead had slain the original Lords and most likely absorbed their souls, their soul would possess immense strength by the time they linked the Flame (if they indeed chose to do so).

title: Projected Heal
snippet:
Projected Heal -  Dark Souls III - spell - description 
 description : A miracle discovered in the last days of Lothric. Toss a light that heals those near the point of impact.

Even those who had forgotten the caress and bounty of the Princess of Sunlight did their best to recall her image. The stories spun about her were most certainly childish, and yet gravely sincere.

title: Cinders of a Lord

title: Dark Soul
snippet: Near the end of the Age of Fire, a slave knight called Gael traveled to the Ringed City, seeking the Pygmy Lords to gain their blood. The blood of the Dark Soul was intended to be used to paint a new Painted World, but to Gael's shock, Filianore's spell was broken and the Pygmy Lords were aged to the point that their blood did not flow, for it was dried in their veins. Even though he knew he had not the strength to survive bearing it, Gael slew the Pygmy Lords and drank from their wounds, absorbing the Dark Soul into himself. It imbued him with a dark miasma and warped his mind, but in the end he was successful, slain by the Ashen One to extract the soul's blood. The current state of the Dark Soul is unknown, but given the eternal nature of Lord Souls, it is unlikely that it was truly destroyed.

title: Lord's Blade Ciaran
snippet: Her weapons were set to appear in *Dark Souls III*, as graphics of their item icon exist within the game files, which is what is used on this very page. They weren't meant to function as they did in *Dark Souls*, as they are displayed together as paired weapons. The reason why they weren't implemented is a mystery.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: The army of Lothric successfully hunted down the wyverns in their region; moreover, by observing how their god commanded such creatures, they even learned how to tame and ride them, and wyverns became a symbol of Lothric alongside its knights. With the wyverns dead or domesticated, the dragonslayers were rendered obsolete, and their armour was retired in favor of lighter, more conventional knight armor. The armour of an ancient Dragonslayer, however, remained in the barracks of the Lothric army, on the bridge between the Altar of Sunlight and the Grand Archives, a monument to the legendary past of Lothric knights.

title: Sir Yorgh
snippet: Some of his men survived the ordeal, escaping from the city and vowing to repent for their misdeeds by founding Lindelt and preserving the doomed city's knowledge. They did so only to clear their conscience, obfuscating the truth of the country's founding and even warping the tale of Sir Yorgh's conceit into one of brave knights defending a country from a terrible dragon.

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : The Soul of Cinder's five-hit combo is reminiscent of Manus's berserker/frenzy combo; both of them juggle the player in the air for the duration of the attack.
Its leggings and shoulder pauldrons look similar to the ones on the Elite Knight Set and the chest piece looks similar to Yhorm's armor. The gauntlets appear identical to Alva's gauntlets, with some noticeable differences.
During the cutscene in Firelink Shrine that takes the player to the kiln, the Fire Keeper will say "Let him/her grant death to the old gods of Lordran, deliverers of the First Flame." This could reference the bosses defeated in the first game, who possessed souls that may have eventually found their way into the fire (if you did not create boss weapons or feed them to Frampt). If that is true, it means that this boss is not only the previous Lords of Cinder, but also every soul that was part of them.

title: Millwood
snippet: Rather than being wiped out, the people of Millwood may have simply abandoned their land en masse; their belongings being left neatly on the ground implies that Midir did not attack to eradicate them. The loss of their sacred tree would have led to the total collapse of their society, to the point where the only thing they could do was leave everything and wander the world, completely lost.

snippet:

 description : An empty head of a white-faced locust that rose from an abyssal swamp.

The white-faced locusts were meant to beckon men to the dark with sermons, but most of them are unable to think past their own stomachs. Someone must rise to the occasion, and restore the path of righteousness.

Perhaps that someone is you? Did you not arise from the Abyss, and did you not resist drowning in the Age of Fire? Locusts and men are kindred spirits.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - location 
 location : Found in the High Wall of Lothric, in the cathedral where Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle resides. Under normal circumstances, she will reveal herself after the player has defeated the first three Lords of Cinder: the Abyss Watchers, Aldrich, Saint of the Deep and Yhorm the Giant.

After the third Lord of Cinder has been defeated, a cutscene will play with Emma summoning the Ashen One to the cathedral. Once there, she will bestow them the Basin of Vows. Walking up to the statue of the beheading knight behind her with it in possession will trigger the boss fight.

Alternatively, the player may kill Emma at any time during the game, loot the basin from her body and approach the statue to commence the battle. This allows for early access to Lothric Castle, the Consumed King's Garden and Untended Graves.

Lord Gwyn, bearer of the ultimate soul, divided that power among his great clan before linking the flame. But he did keep his crown, perhaps to preserve a symbol of the monarch, for its actual power had fully subsided.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: In the heyday of Lothric, when the descendants of Drangleic and followers of the Way of Blue and the Heirs of the Sun moved to another location, they still remembered the Nameless King as their God of the Sun. As the early inhabitants of Lothric found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns, they had to become dragonslayers to survive; and so they turned to the Nameless King, building an altar for him. The first knights of Lothric devoted themselves to the worship of the ancestral deity of the sun and war, who in return gave them the tools to face the wyverns. Their first armors were heavy masses of iron capable of withstanding dragon fire and similar in design to the ancient armor of the dragonslayers of Anor Londo, while their shields were capable of absorbing the fierce lightning attacks of wyverns. From the sun god they also soon learned how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons. Finally

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - rings 
 rings : Each of the Four Knights was gifted a unique ring imbued with special powers. The Chosen Undead can find them scattered throughout Lordran, and their item descriptions give minor insight into who the knights were and what they did.

title: Londor
snippet: These pilgrims of Londor, whose humanity had accumulated and stagnated inside their body during their journey, underwent a peculiar transformation upon death. As time passed, their corpses would grow and evolve into a new form of sentient life, similar in appearance to a humanoid insect. These humanoid "Pilgrim Pupa" were harmless on their own, but were capable of manifesting and controlling physical bodies known as Angels: These aerial creatures were adorned with large, brilliant wings, and could unleash lethal rays of light. Some Pilgrims, however, seemingly did not turn into Pupae that conceive Angels, and instead became similar entities known as Pilgrim Butterflies. These twisted beings are only vaguely similar to the Angels, and continue their progenitors' journey towards upper Lothric, populating the skies of Lothric Castle. Some Pilgrim Butterflies are even capable of taking symbiotic hosts in other beings similar to the Pupae and their Angels; however, the lives of the

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Soul of Cinder is the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame through history, becoming Lords of Cinder, and thus is an entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Champions despite just being an empty husk.

It exists as the Flame's last defense inside its Kiln, protecting it from anyone attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength—a role that it has enacted for a very long time, confronting all who entered the Kiln as aspiring Lords.

When tested by an aspiring Champion, the Soul of Cinder would even bring out the remnants of the will and power of the first one to ever link the First Flame: Lord Gwyn himself.

She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace.  strategy : In human form, it is possible to have Solaire of Astora and/or Knight Lautrec of Carim assist during this battle, although Lautrec must be freed and spoken to in Firelink Shrine first. Their summon signs are found just before the white light leading to the Gargoyles. Summoning both knights and simply mobbing each Gargoyle can lead to a quick and relatively painless victory.

The fight is beset by the constant danger of falling off (target-locking, coupled with the camera angle and narrow field of view, can make it hard to track the player character's footing) and facing off against a single gargoyle on top of the church roof. Trying to circle the gargoyle while holding up a shield is a good way to avoid its long-reaching frontal attacks. If the gargoyle takes off, move away or get ready to dodge its plunging attack.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Once the first gargoyle is cut down to half its health, the second gargoyle will join the fight. Fortunately, this gargoyle is already severely injured (it arrives at half-health). It has the same attacks as the first gargoyle minus those that involve flying or using the tail.

Players having difficulty managing their positioning against the two gargoyles should save any consumables (ex., Fire Bombs) until the first gargoyle's health is approaching 50%, and then use them to finish it off as quickly as possible. For as long as both gargoyles are alive, players should keep them both on the screen; if not feasible, one can try following audio cues to perceive an oncoming attack. The use of Gold Pine Resin and other weapon enhancements can greatly help in finishing off the first gargoyle, and make the overall fight significantly easier.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Both Gargoyles wield halberds and can breathe fire, although the first gargoyle usually will only breathe fire after the second one jumps down. A fire-resistant shield such as the Black Knight Shield (and, optionally, fire-resistant armor) can be very useful, as the fire breath covers a wide area. While breathing fire, the gargoyles won't move, making it the perfect opportunity to run over and hit them from behind (this makes avoiding or blocking the fire twice as important, as its stagger effect will consume precious seconds, limiting the time available to attack the gargoyles).

The first gargoyle's tail can be severed to gain a weapon (Gargoyle Tail Axe).

title: Bell Keeper Bow
snippet:
Bell Keeper Bow -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Bell Keeper Bow is a rather unusual bow, to say the least.

For starters, it is the *lightest* bow available in the game, weighing in at 0.5 units, making it a prime candidate for lightweight builds, or players trying to not over-encumber themselves.

It also has extremely-low requirements to be used effectively, as it requires a measly 4 strength (in reality, it requires **2 strength** as bows must be held with both hands) to be held, and 11 dexterity to use.

It has fair range, much long the Long Bow, yet it handles very poorly, as the draw time to fire an arrow is much longer than average; this is not quite as slow as the Dragonrider Bow's handling, however. It also scales worse than the Longbow, and has significantly lower base damage (55/110 as opposed to 75/150).

title: Bell Keeper Bow
snippet: Overall, this bow is interesting in multiple aspects, but far from ideal for practical use, as there are far better bows out there that handle better and boast greater damage to boot. It is best to avoid using this bow unless you are at the peak of your equipment load (70.0%), and require a ranged weapon that is very lightweight.

title: Bell Keeper of Alken
snippet:
It is likely that Venn once stood where Belfy Sol does; as Belfry Sol, which the Bell Keeper calls "Arken", is atop the Iron Keep, it is possible that the Prince was a member of the Old Iron King's family, perhaps the Old Iron King himself as he was in a loveless marriage to Mytha because he "had feelings for another". The original goal of the Bell Keepers might have been to somehow preserve the love affair between the Old Iron King and the Princess of Ven, or its memory.

It is unclear if the Bell Keeper Dark Spirit that can invade the player in Belfry Luna is the same as the Bell Keeper NPC; unlike the regular Bell Keeper enemies, who wear full helmets, the invader wears the same partial helmet as the NPC that lets most of his face apparent.

title: Bell Keeper of Alken
snippet:
Bell Keeper of Alken -  Dark Souls II - character - lead 
 lead : For the enemy that can be found in the same locations, see Bell Keeper (enemy). For the invading Dark Spirit in Belfry Luna, see Bell Keeper (Dark Spirit)*.
The **Bell Keeper of Alken**, also known as the **Bell Keeper of Venn**, is a character in *Dark Souls II*. He is voiced by Jason Pitt, who also voiced Vengarl of Forossa, Satsuki in *Demon's Souls* and Valtr, Master of the League in *Bloodborne*.

The leader of the Bell Keepers covenant, he can found in both areas protected by its members, Belfry Luna and Belfry Sol.

title: Bell Keeper of Alken
snippet:
Bell Keeper of Alken -  Dark Souls II - character - plot 
 plot : He is the leader of Bell Keepers covenant, which the player can join by talking to him. He will also provide rewards upon ranking up in the covenant. He also warns the player not to touch the bell he's protecting, or his minion will chop them to pieces.

Because the Bell Keeper has little sanity, it is unclear how much his dialogue can be trusted, but it hints that there might in fact be two distinct Bell Keepers, one in Luna and one and Sol, as in Luna he will claim that "the Princess" made him "To guard the Bell of Alken! In Alken!" while, in Sol, he claims that "the Prince" made him, "To guard the Bell of Venn! In Venn!". Killing the Bell Keeper in either location leads to the absence of the Bell Keeper from the other, further hinting at a direct connection and possibly towards them being the same person.

title: Bell Keeper's Seal
snippet:
Bell Keeper's Seal -  Dark Souls II - ring - description 
 description : Ring of the Bell Keeper covenant.

Join this covenant and wear this ring to be automatically summoned to the world of an invader of the bell keepers' domain.

The twin bells symbolize the bond between two lovers who could never be united. The bell keepers are their eternal guardians. For that is their love; that is their curse.

title: Bell Keeper's Seal
snippet:
Bell Keeper's Seal -  Dark Souls II - ring - effect 
 effect : Wearing this ring allows the player to invade another player who is either in Belfry Luna or Belfry Sol. Anyone's world can be invaded by a Bell Keeper, included fellow covenant members' worlds.

If worn in one of the belfries, the player will only invade trespassers in the same belfry as they currently are.

title: Bell Keeper's Seal

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Bell Keepers -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : After joining the covenant and receiving the ring, the player will automatically invade other worlds while they are wearing it. The player does not need to be in either belfry to be eligible for summoning, they can be almost anywhere in the world other than Majula and Things Betwixt, as denoted by the Bell Keepers' badge on the heads-up display with a glowing effect animation.

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Bell Keepers -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Usually the members of the Bell Keepers covenant will invade players with ease and they tend to bunch up, to a maximum number of three, frequently outnumbering the host. At this point either two things happen: the Bell Keepers decide to work together and will most likely kill the player; or they battle each other for the host kill.
Though you can be summoned as gray spirit from any area in the world, you have a much higher chance if you are inside Belfry or it's governing area (Lost Bastille or Iron Keep).

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Bell Keepers -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : To join the Bell Keepers, the player must speak to the Bell Keeper of Alken at the entrance of Belfry Luna or Belfry Sol. Exhausting his dialogue will allow the player to join the covenant and accepting will have them recieve the Bell Keeper's Seal.

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Achieving victories over other players in the belfries will cause a player in the Bell Keepers to advance in the covenant. Upon defeating a trespassing player, the Bell Keeper member will get sent back to their world with a Titanite Chunk. A member of the covenant can also gain victories by defeating a rarely-spawning enemy in Belfry Sol, named the Mad Warrior. This makes the Bell Keepers one of the few covenants that can be ranked up while in offline mode.

Ranking up in this Covenant is the only way to get access to the Sorcery Hidden Weapon.

title: Bell Keepers
snippet: The goal of the player while invading is to protect Belfry Luna and Belfry Sol from trespassers, including invading Blue Arbiter Spirits and summoned Phantoms. Despite being a part of the covenant, the player will still be invaded by other Bell Keeper members, and the dwarven protectors in these places are still hostile. However, while the player is invading, the enemies will be non-aggressive and any other Bell Keepers summoned to invade will be allies. All summoned Bell Keeper members will appear as grey phantoms, and up to two Bell Keeper phantoms (three in ) can be summoned at a time.

title: Bellowing Dragoncrest Ring (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Bellowing Dragoncrest Ring (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - ring - availability 
 availability : Found in the Irithyll Dungeon. Requires the Jailbreaker's Key.

Proceed straight ahead until reaching the end of the corridor on the upper floor and unlock the barred window at the end. The ring can be looted from a corpse lying on one of the rock ledges accessed afterward.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - quelaag_s_domain_bell 
 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The Bells of Awakening are hinted at being the first destination of the Chosen Undead and, when rung, the fate of the undead shall be known. Upon arriving in Firelink Shrine, the Crestfallen Warrior informs the player that there are, in fact, two Bells of Awakening. One up above and one far below. This is essentially all the instruction and plot that is revealed upon arrival in Lordran.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Ringing the bell in Quelaag's Domain first will have no different effect than if the player rang the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] first. Although this will cause Lautrec's questline to progress, leading to the death of Anastacia.
The Bells of Awakening were used to awaken Kingseeker Frampt and open the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - undead_church_bell 
 undead_church_bell : One of the Bells is located in the Undead Parish, up above from Firelink Shrine. After dispatching the Bell Gargoyles, the Chosen Undead is able to climb to the top of the Church Belltower and ring the Bell of Awakening.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - notes 
 notes : In the Prepare to Die Edition, online players in the vicinity of the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] were able to hear the bell being rung from other player worlds. This wasn’t the case for the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Bell in Quelaag’s Domain].
In the remastered version of the game, online players are now able to hear either the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] or the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s domain Bell] being rung from other player worlds while exploring one area or the other . (as the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s Bell] toll was specifically added in the remaster)

title: Firelink Altar
snippet:
Firelink Altar -  Dark Souls - location - general_information 
 general_information : It is here that the player places the Lordvessel on the Altar and fills it with the various Lord Souls in order to access the Kiln of the First Flame to confront Gwyn, Lord of Cinder.

The altar automatically grants players ten Estus Flask uses by itself, twenty when Anastacia has been resurrected, without the requirement of kindling when rested at.

title: Firelink Altar
snippet:
Firelink Altar -  Dark Souls - location - description 
 description : The Firelink Altar can only be accessed via "warping" with either Kingseeker Frampt or Darkstalker Kaathe, or by jumping into Frampt's pit, once the Lordvessel is obtained.

If the player chooses to aid one of the Primordial Serpents, then they must "entrust their flesh" with one, be swallowed whole, and regurgitated onto a large platform of similar material to the structures in Lost Izalith, surrounded by large roots. Alternatively, if the player chooses to jump into the pit, they will land safely onto the shrine.
